curated.instructions: omr/instructions/9392-1-2.pdf (the quad bike the file builds, with the chain and the yellow single-cylinder engine, "66" on the box); omr/instructions/9392-1-1.pdf builds the other quad bike ("99")

functions.does: Turning the handlebars steers the front wheels: the steering column turns an arm at its foot, which pushes the two steering links to the front hubs.
functions.source: book: steps 15-16 (steering column, pages 38-39) and step 33 (handlebars, page 56); the links and hubs on pages 33-37

functions.does: Rolling the quad works the engine: the rear axle's sprocket drives a chain forward to a cross shaft, whose gear turns the crankshaft, and the yellow piston pumps up and down in its cylinder.
functions.source: book: steps 5-7 (rear axle and sprocket, page 7 arrow shows the axle turning), sub-steps 1-5 and steps 23-25 (engine, crankshaft and gears, pages 44-48), step 26 (the 26-link chain, page 49)

functions.does: The engine can also be turned from its crankshaft, turning the rear wheels through the gears and chain.
functions.source: inferred: the drive train has nothing that stops it running backwards

functions.does: The rear wheels ride on a swinging arm with a single shock absorber: pushing the rear axle up swings the arm about its pivot behind the engine and squeezes the shock absorber; the chain runs along the arm.
functions.source: book: steps 1-13 (rear axle and swinging arm) and the side views on pages 26 and 41

functions.does: The front wheels have independent suspension: each hub rides between an upper and a lower suspension arm with a shock absorber, and moves up and down, steering as it goes.
functions.source: book: steps 10-14 (suspension arms, hubs and shock absorbers, pages 33-37); inferred: that it's meant to move

functions.does: The three shock absorbers' springs hold the quad up and spring back.
functions.source: book: steps 10-14 and the rear shock absorber on page 4
functions.skip: springs only push back under force

questions.question: Does the rear chain stay meshed as the swing arm moves?
